rationale: This is a cosmetic re-timing of the archived "Undermaintenance Profit Erosion" (same profitability gate, same capex-minus-depreciation leg, with the 3-year profitability trend swapped for a 1-year delta and both legs lagged), so it is effectively a rediscovery of an already-tested signal rather than a new mechanism.

The volatility leg is a near-substitute for the archived and unsuccessful "Profitable Capex Instability," and the combination of profitability conditioning with earnings volatility and capital intensity largely re-packages the well-documented earnings-volatility/asset-tangibility anomalies rather than testing a genuinely new interaction.

This is the archived "Profitable Inventory Divergence" — the pair's strongest result — with the gate and inventory leg lagged one year; the shift adds a plausible timing story but is too close to the original to count as a distinct test, and inventory growth is itself a canonical published anomaly.

The cash-depletion leg is a genuinely new ingredient relative to the archived post-peak capex signals and the sign logic is internally consistent, but the four-way conjunction (gate plus triple MIN) risks thin, unstable extreme portfolios and a large indicator-induced mass at zero, so coverage and turnover diagnostics must be checked carefully.

Mechanically coherent and sign-consistent, but it is the third variant of the same profitable-borrower/interest-expense theme that already yielded essentially zero FF5 alpha twice, and the second leg is contaminated by the profit-deterioration channel (a firm with falling oibdp and flat xint scores high), so it partly re-tests earnings decline rather than debt service.

Replacing the failed amortization-gap leg with a change in SG&A intensity is a substantively different cost channel rather than a cosmetic tweak, though ΔSG&A-to-sales overlaps the long-known Abarbanell–Bushee fundamental-signal literature, so the novelty rests mainly on the conditional interaction with intangible accumulation.
